title: Admission to the Vault and the Opening of a Leased Safe Deposit Box
content:
Only the lessee, a co-lessee and named deputies may enter the vault holding Safe Deposit Boxes. Each presents government photo identification on entry, and the entry is logged with the name exactly as it appears on that identification.

## The standing of the rental

Vault access is allowed only while the rental is active.

The standing is settled by the bank's own record of that rental, read before entry and matched to the rental whose box is to be opened. A rental standing waitlisted, past due, pending drilling or closed does not admit entry.

## Opening the box

Opening the box needs both the bank's guard key and the lessee's own key. Neither key opens the door by itself.

## When the vault may be entered

Entry is during branch lobby hours. An appointment outside lobby hours exists only for a size for which such an appointment is offered, and carries the after-hours appointment charge set for that size as a service charge on the rental.

## Points of judgement

A person who is neither the lessee, nor the co-lessee recorded on the rental, nor one of the deputies named on it, is not admitted to the box, whatever their relation to the lessee and whatever they bring with them.

The name written in the entry log is the name as it stands on the identification presented, not the name the person gives at the counter and not the name as it stands on the rental.

Three conditions are separate and each must hold in its own right: the person is one of those named on the rental, that person presents government photo identification, and the rental stands active.
